title: Where is leaf 170 of the Archimedes Palimpsest?
short: A 1906 photograph identifies the missing leaf. Where did it go, and what readings might the physical page still preserve?
matters: Locating the leaf could recover text or correct readings obscured in the old photograph. The case also offers a way to recognize a dispersed manuscript leaf even if it has acquired a different description.
stuck: The photograph shows wording, ruling and damage. An auction entry or catalogue may show only one side or describe the leaf under its later prayer text.
solved: Match an independently located leaf to the photograph through the placement of text, ruling and defects, then verify and publish its provenance.
approach: Trace former owner Anne Guersan’s correspondence and compare candidate leaves with the 1906 image, allowing for rotations, later additions and cropping.
